transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Rajiv Patel (CTO), Elena Morales (Head of ML), Tom Baxter (Infra Lead), Lisa Ng (Security), Markus Lee (Product)
Shared artifacts: dedicated_pricing_v2.xlsx (Maya), security_summary_link (Maya), sample-traffic-template.xlsx (customer)

Summary: Quick discovery focused on Hightower Bank's interest in Redwood Dedicated for customer-facing LLM features. Primary concerns: strict data isolation, predictable latency and throughput, burst handling for end-of-day batch spikes, and compliance (SOC2/KMS/SAML). Discussed expected traffic, GPU types (A100 vs H100), autoscaling/burst strategies, KV cache and warm-up, monitoring and SLOs, and next steps for pricing and a benchmarking pilot.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I think we have about 45 minutes, um, so quick round of intros?
[00:08] Rajiv Patel: Rajiv here, CTO. We run a bunch of customer-facing features, looking at switching from a mix of API-hosted to dedicated.
[00:15] Elena Morales: Elena, Head of ML, we own model infra and evals.
[00:18] Tom Baxter: Tom, infra. Curious about network isolation and burst behaviour.
[00:22] Lisa Ng: Lisa from security — SOC2 questions, KMS, audit logs.
[00:26] Maya Chen: Great; from Redwood, Daniel our SE will handle the deep infra questions.
[00:29] Daniel Ortiz: Hi all, thanks. Quick agenda: figure out workload shape, SLOs, isolation requirements, and talk config + pricing for Dedicated.

[01:05] Maya Chen: Rajiv, can you walk through the use case and why dedicated vs hosted?
[01:12] Rajiv Patel: Sure. We want deterministic latency for our virtual assistant and a couple of generation features in mobile apps. Hosted API has worked for dev but with unpredictable cold-starts and token costs. For regs we need data not leaving our VPC, so Dedicated with private deployment looks like the move.
[01:32] Markus Lee: Also concerned about end-of-day batch jobs — we have spikes during statements processing and marketing sends. Need burst capacity.

[02:10] Daniel Ortiz: When you say deterministic, what's your p95 target and typical request size?
[02:15] Elena Morales: P95 around 350-450ms for single-turn chat responses, about 250-800 tokens per request (avg ~320). Peak qps is roughly 30 req/s, but during spikes it can be 120 req/s for 10-20 minutes, and some nightly batches of 6k concurrent small requests.
[02:36] Tom Baxter: We also have throughput requirements for embeddings — batch embed jobs of 200k rows overnight. Latency less critical there.

[03:05] Daniel Ortiz: Good detail. Our Dedicated offering lets you pin GPUs and have reserved capacity; autoscale/burst can be configured with reserved baseline plus burst pool. For the 120 req/s spike, we usually recommend a baseline fleet sized for steady-state and a burst pool for 2x-4x short bursts.
[03:26] Rajiv Patel: What's the cost tradeoff — reserve a big fleet vs rely on burst?
[03:31] Maya Chen: Pricing spreadsheet we shared shows baseline reserved pricing and separate burst pricing. Bursts are billed at a premium but avoid over-committing. We can show examples for A100 vs H100; H100 gives better perf per GPU but pricing and availability differ.

[04:10] Elena Morales: Also curious about quantization and model variants — we plan to run an open model and a tuned variant. Can you support multiple pinned model versions on the same Dedicated pool?
[04:21] Daniel Ortiz: Yes, you can pin model versions and route requests by policy. One GPU pool can host multiple model variants with memory planning; if you need strict isolation per model, we can carve separate pools. Sometimes teams use lighter quantized variants for high throughput and a higher-accuracy full-precision variant as fallback.

[05:02] Lisa Ng: Security: we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, customer-managed KMS, and the control plane must not have direct access to PII. Do you support private control plane and on-prem options?
[05:16] Maya Chen: Yes — Redwood Private and Dedicated both have VPC options. For enterprise Dedicated we can enable private control plane and support KMS integrations plus audit log exports. We'll share SOC2 docs and a security whitepaper.

[06:00] Tom Baxter: Network-wise, can we keep traffic inside our VPC? We want no egress to public internet for inference data.
[06:07] Daniel Ortiz: Absolutely — VPC peering or VPC-only endpoints are supported. For on-prem air-gapped, we have a package but that is a different procurement track.

[06:40] Markus Lee: On warm-up: our mobile product is latency-sensitive; cold starts when a model swaps can add 800ms-1.2s. How do you handle KV cache warm-up and batching warmup?
[06:52] Daniel Ortiz: We use continuous KV cache and pre-warming strategies. If you pin the model variant and keep a small warm pool, cold starts are minimal. Also prefix caching and request-level caching for repeated prompts helps. We'll propose a warm pool config in the benchmark plan.

[07:30] Elena Morales: For embeddings overnight, do you recommend separate dedicated infra or run on same pool as chat?
[07:37] Daniel Ortiz: Often embeddings are batched on cheaper quantized instances or scheduled on a separate pool to avoid interfering with chat SLOs. You can also use job queues and autoscaling policies to budget.

[08:05] Rajiv Patel: GPU choices — between A100 and H100, what's the practical diff for our workload?
[08:13] Daniel Ortiz: H100 shows better throughput for LLMs at scale and lower cost per token in many cases, but A100s are still common and sometimes more available. For 800-token average requests and p95 targets you described, H100s with bfloat or TF32/FP16 plus quantization will reduce token latency. We'll model both in the pricing sheet.

[09:00] Tom Baxter: Observability — we need token-level cost breakouts, per-route latency dashboards, tracing hooks and alerts on regressions.
[09:09] Maya Chen: Redwood Console provides per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost, and tracing. We also support integration with your monitoring (Datadog, Prometheus).

[09:30] Lisa Ng: On compliance, is there an audit trail for admin actions? We need to show who accessed keys and made config changes.
[09:38] Daniel Ortiz: Yes, audit logs for control plane actions and API accesses can be exported to your SIEM; RBAC is supported. We'll send sample audit schema.

[10:15] Markus Lee: Hypothetical numbers — if we want p95 400ms and sustain 30 qps steady with spikes to 120 qps, what fleet size do you recommend?
[10:25] Daniel Ortiz: Ballpark: for H100, maybe 6-8 GPUs baseline for steady 30 qps depending on batching and request length; add a burst pool of 6-10 GPUs for short spikes. We'll run a benchmark with your traffic to refine that. For A100s, you'd need ~1.5x GPUs.

[11:00] Elena Morales: Benchmarking — what do you need from us?
[11:04] Daniel Ortiz: A sample traffic profile (timestamps, payload sizes), a set of prompts for quality/regression checks, and any PII redaction rules. We'll run 1:1 parity tests and a multi-tenant simulation for burst tests.

[11:35] Rajiv Patel: Contract/SLAs — what uptime and latency SLAs are typical?
[11:41] Maya Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA backing for uptime and configurable latency targets at the plan level; we'll outline SLA tiers in the pricing doc. Enterprise contracts include support response times.

[12:10] Markus Lee: Any caveats around autoscaling — how fast can you scale from baseline to burst?
[12:15] Daniel Ortiz: Burst scale speed depends on whether burst pool is warm or cold. Warm burst pools (standby VMs/GPU instances) can absorb within 20-60s; cold starts can take several minutes. We recommend a warm pool sized for your typical spike profile.

[13:00] Tom Baxter: For embeddings job of 200k rows overnight, any rough ETA?
[13:06] Daniel Ortiz: If you batch effectively and use quantized instances, that could be done within a few hours on a separate pool; we'll put numbers in the benchmark plan once we know model and batch sizes.

[13:32] Lisa Ng: Data retention and logs — can we configure retention windows?
[13:36] Maya Chen: Yes, retention windows for request logs and KV caches are configurable; we support auto-delete and export to your storage.

[14:05] Elena Morales: One more on failover — if a region has capacity constraints, does Redwood auto-failover to another region/model variant?
[14:13] Daniel Ortiz: Smart routing supports region fallback and compatible model variants; you can set policy to prefer same-region or fail to a cheaper hosted variant. Failover behavior is configurable per-route.

[15:00] Maya Chen: Okay, let's recap next steps — I'll send the pricing spreadsheet and security docs, Daniel will prepare a benchmark plan and recommend GPU sizing and warm pool config, Elena will share traffic profile. We'll aim to schedule the benchmark week of Jan 4.
[15:25] Rajiv Patel: Sounds good. One note — legal will want the private control plane details; Lisa will follow up on requirements.
[15:35] Lisa Ng: Yep, we'll need the security whitepaper and SOC2 report.
[15:40] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone; we'll follow up via email and add the benchmark invite.
[15:45] Elena Morales: Thanks, bye.
[15:46] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings for acronyms — "KV cache" appears as "K V cache" in a couple places, and some speaker labels slightly off during crosstalk.

End of artifact.
